data.description:
Deine Aufgaben

mammaly ist eine zertifizierte B Corp. Nachhaltigkeit ist bei uns kein Nebenthema, sondern gehört zu unserem Selbstverständnis. Du verantwortest unser ESG-Management von der B-Corp-Zertifizierung bis zur CO₂-Bilanz. Außerdem arbeitest du direkt unserem COO zu und treibst die Weiterentwicklung seiner Bereiche und strategischen Projekte voran, mit Schwerpunkt Retail.

Projekte & COO Office (ca. 70 %)* Du arbeitest direkt unserem COO zu, bei der Weiterentwicklung seiner Bereiche und strategischen Projekte, mit Schwerpunkt Retail-Entwicklung.

  • Du steuerst bereichsübergreifende Projekte, zum Beispiel neue Handelspartner, Sortiments- und Channel-Themen, und hältst sie nach.
  • Du bereitest Entscheidungen vor: Analysen, Business Cases, KPI-Reportings.
  • Du bereitest Management-, Board- und Partnertermine vor und nach.
  • Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen Retail, SCM, Marketing und Finance und sorgst dafür, dass Dinge vorankommen.

ESG & Nachhaltigkeit (ca. 30 %)* Du verantwortest unsere B-Corp-Zertifizierung: Du pflegst das B Impact Assessment, bereitest die Rezertifizierung vor und setzt die neuen B-Lab-Standards um.

  • Du entwickelst unsere Nachhaltigkeitsstrategie weiter und setzt sie um, mit Fokus auf Supply Chain, Lieferanten und Verpackung.
  • Du erstellst und aktualisierst unsere CO₂-Bilanz (Scope 1–3) und leitest Reduktionsmaßnahmen ab.
  • Du beantwortest Nachhaltigkeitsanfragen von Handelspartnern und Investoren (Fragebögen, Ratings, Reportings).
  • Du behältst regulatorische Entwicklungen im Blick, etwa die EU-Verpackungsverordnung, Vorgaben zu Umweltaussagen und CSRD/VSME, und stellst die Einhaltung sicher.
  • Du verankerst Nachhaltigkeit im Team, zum Beispiel über Schulungen, interne Kommunikation und Impact-Themen.

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium in Nachhaltigkeitsmanagement, Umweltwissenschaften, BWL oder einem verwandten Fach
  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Nachhaltigkeits- bzw. ESG-Management, idealerweise in FMCG, Food oder Pet
  • Erfahrung mit B Corp (B Impact Assessment, Zertifizierung) und CO₂-Bilanzierung
  • Erfahrung im Projektmanagement; idealerweise hast du schon eng mit der Geschäftsführung zusammengearbeitet
  • Analytisch, strukturiert, hands-on
  • Souveräner Auftritt gegenüber Management, Handelspartnern und Lieferanten

data.title: Office Manager / Office Operations Support (w/m/d)
data.description:
Über IONOS

Bei IONOS verwalten wir nicht nur Server, wir prägen mit unseren Lösungen die digitale Zukunft für über 6,2 Millionen Kundinnen und Kunden weltweit. Als Europas führender Hosting-Anbieter und Pionier für unabhängige Cloud-Lösungen bauen wir eine Infrastruktur der nächsten Generation: von souveränen Cloud-Architekturen und hochperformanten GPU-Clustern bis hin zu integrierten KI-Automatisierungstools.

Was uns antreibt: Digitale Entscheidungsfreiheit für Europa und echter Impact für kleine und mittlere Unternehmen (KMU) sowie Großunternehmen. Wir arbeiten in agilen Teams, setzen auf transparente Strukturen und glauben daran, dass Exzellenz und Innovation nur mit echtem Teamgeist entstehen.

Bereit für Deinen nächsten Schritt? Werde ein Teil von IONOS und wachse mit uns.

Aufgabenbereich

Bei IONOS bringst Du täglich Ordnung in die Dinge, die zählen – und das buchstäblich. Als Office Manager oder Office Operations Support bist Du das Herzstück unseres Büros: die erste Anlaufstelle für Kolleg:innen, Dienstleister und Gäste. Du schaffst eine Arbeitsumgebung, in der sich alle wohlfühlen, Prozesse reibungslos laufen und nichts dem Zufall überlassen wird.

  • Empfang & Gästebetreuung: Du bist das freundliche Gesicht unseres Unternehmens – Du empfängst Gäste und Besucher:innen professionell, koordinierst Meetingräume und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Mitarbeitenden jederzeit einen gut organisierten Anlaufpunkt vorfinden.
  • Büroorganisation & Logistik: Du planst und optimierst eigenständig die Bestände an Büromaterialien, Verbrauchsgütern und Cateringartikeln (Kaffee, Getränke, Snacks, Sanitärprodukte) – mit Blick auf Effizienz und Verfügbarkeit. Außerdem koordinierst Du die gesamte ein- und ausgehende Paket- und Postlogistik, einschließlich komplexer Sendungen und IT-Hardware-Versand.
  • Infrastruktur & Facility Management: Du bist die zentrale Schnittstelle zum Gebäudemanagement und zu externen Dienstleistern: Du überwachst Wartungspläne, koordinierst Reparaturen und sorgst dafür, dass unser Büro stets in einwandfreiem Zustand ist. data.title: Senior B2B Sales Manager
data.description:
YOUR FUTURE, ON DEMAND

The ideal blend of stability and flexibility. A genuinely human employer that cares for people and the planet. True autonomy to shape what comes next, for us and you. This is the perfect platform to take your career where you want.

Back in 2005, we pioneered Europe’s first TV streaming service. Today, we're a leading TV streaming provider with millions of monthly users, and since 2021 we've been ClimatePartner-certified. Over 200 colleagues of 47 nationalities. We’re the grown-up start-up, helping to shape a better future since day one.That hasn’t changed, even if the world has. We’re friendly, international, inclusive – and our people say we’re reliable and transparent, too. It’s why they trust us and believe in what we do.

THE ROLE

Make Zattoo the TV platform partner of choice for operators and broadcasters in Eastern and Northern Europe. This role turns new markets into lasting revenue and shapes Zattoo’s next stage of growth. You will join a close-knit team working across Germany and Switzerland that values trust, collaboration and hands-on ownership over hierarchy and heavy process.

THE TEAM

The Zattoo Business Sales Team is responsible for all sales activities related to Zattoo’s TV-as-a-Service and streaming technology offerings, including the End-to-End TV platform as well as Modular products such as Streaming, Ingest and Orchestration solutions. We work closely with Product, Portfolio Management, Marketing, Client Success and Project Management to bring complex solutions to market and build long-term customer relationships across different regions and customer segments.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Build a new business pipeline across Eastern and Northern Europe and win telcos, ISPs, broadcasters and OTT platforms as long-term customers
  • Own complex, high-value deals end-to-end, from first conversation to signed contract
  • Navigate long decision cycles and orchestrate our Sales Engineering, Product and Legal teams to get deals over the line
  • Build lasting relationships with senior decision makers up to C-level
  • Shape tailored offers from our modular platform (INGEST, STREAM, ORCHESTRATE, E2E)
  • Be Zattoo’s face in your markets, at customer meetings, trade shows and partner events, and bring market insights back to Product

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

Experience required (Must-have)

  • 10+ years in B2B enterprise sales, closing complex deals with long sales cycles
  • Proven track record selling to telcos, broadcasters, media companies or platform providers
  • Deep understanding of the TV, OTT and streaming market
  • Established network in Eastern and/or Northern European markets
  • Confident negotiating with C-level and procurement teams
  • Business fluent English

Nice to have

  • Language skills in one or more Eastern or Northern European languages
  • Experience selling modular tech or SaaS platforms
  • German language skills are advantageous

Behavioural Competencies

  • Ownership: Takes full responsibility for their markets and deals, without relying on a large sales support machine.
  • Honest Forecasting: Reports pipeline and forecast realistically and transparently, including bad news early.
  • Team Player: Works closely with Product, Sales Engineering and Legal and values collaboration over individual heroics.
  • Hands-on Mentality: Comfortable building structures and materials themselves where needed.
  • Long-term Thinking: Builds relationships for the long run instead of chasing quick wins.

WHY JOIN US?

At Zattoo, you’re always on firm ground with real freedom to explore. You’ll have the support and opportunity you need to go far, while you’re helping us create a sustainable and entertainment-filled future for all.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

  • Reward: strong market competitive salary
  • Recharge: 30 days vacation plus public holidays
  • Regulate: trust based flexible working hours and the option for remote work worldwide for up to 8 weeks per year

Plus:

  • We’re sharing: Free access to the best streaming experience on the market
  • We're developing: Your own development budget, German classes and Zattoo all-company hack days
  • We’re inclusive: ‘Zattooies’ are a fun, engaged, and diverse team made up of 47 nationalities
  • We’re healthy: Health checks, mental wellbeing support, team sports and more!
  • We’re mobile: Discounted BVG tickets and free bike rentals
  • We’re sociable: A calendar of events with fireside chats, lunches, in-house bar, BBQ’s, monthly socials, summer party and an annual off-site event

Zattoo enables our users to view indiscriminately and we reflect that in our team too. Regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability or any other characteristic protected by law we encourage everyone to apply and will give everyone equal consideration. We are an equal opportunities employer — join us and help build a diverse team dedicated to revolutionising the way you watch TV.

We are committed to ensuring fair, open, and equitable hiring practices and are happy to answer any questions you may have about us or the role throughout the whole process. In line with the EU Pay Transparency Directive, we share the applicable compensation range with you before your first interview.

data.title: Marketing Lead
data.description:
Über YLAB

Wir bauen die KI, die wir unseren eigenen Kindern geben würden.

Kinder wachsen heute mit KI auf. Wir sorgen dafür, dass diese KI neugierig macht statt süchtig, sicher ist statt datenhungrig und für Kinder gebaut wird statt für Erwachsene.

Wir sind YLAB, ein kleines KI-Lab aus Köln-Ehrenfeld. Wir entwickeln Software und Hardware aus einer Hand, vom Sprachmodell bis zum Gehäuse. Unser erstes Produkt ist Onoo, ein Lernbegleiter ohne Bildschirm für Kinder ab vier. Onoo fragt zurück, lässt raten und denkt mit. Er hat keine Kamera und kein Display, zeigt keine Werbung und verkauft keine Daten.

Warum YLAB

Deine Arbeit landet im Kinderzimmer, nicht in einem Dashboard.

Software & Hardware: KI, App, Firmware und Gerät entstehen bei uns zusammen. Du siehst, wie aus Code etwas wird, das ein Kind in die Hand nimmt.

Du arbeitest an echten offenen Fragen, zum Beispiel wie KI Kinderstimmen versteht und Fünfjährigen die Welt erklärt.

Tech, Pädagogik und Forschung sitzen bei uns an einem Tisch.

Ehrlichkeit statt Hochglanz: Vieles bauen wir zum ersten Mal. Wenn dich das reizt, sollten wir reden.

Was wir bieten

  • Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Du bekommst echte Themen und Probleme statt Tickets, und deine Entscheidungen haben Gewicht.

  • Top Arbeitsmaterial: Du arbeitest mit dem Setup und den Tools, die du brauchst.

  • Flexible Weiterbildung: Konferenz, Kurs oder Workshop – du sagst uns, was dich weiterbringt.

  • Hybrid mit Herz: Remote, wenn du Ruhe brauchst, und im Office, wenn wir gemeinsam tüfteln.

Über die Rolle

Unser erstes Produkt ist Onoo: ein kleiner, bildschirmfreier KI-Freund, der Kindern zwischen 4 und 9 ihre Warum-Fragen beantwortet. Der Prototyp funktioniert, der Launch ist 2027. Jetzt brauchen wir jemanden, der Onoo in die Köpfe und Wohnzimmer von Eltern bringt.

Du bist unsere erste Marketing-Person, mit Platz am Gründertisch. Keine Agentur, kein Team unter dir, keine fertigen Prozesse. Du baust Marke, Community und Funnel von null auf – erst mit den eigenen Händen, dann mit einem Team.

Was dich erwartet: ein Hardware-Produkt plus Abo, Direktvertrieb in DACH und Eltern als Zielgruppe, die das Beste für ihre Kinder wollen und Datenschutz ernst nehmen. Und ein Thema, bei dem KI und Kinder in einem Satz stehen. Da gewinnt, wer Vertrauen aufbauen kann.

Wie du uns helfen kannst

  • Du machst aus Onoo eine Marke, die Eltern sofort verstehen: Positionierung, Story, Ton – vom Video bis zum Karton.

  • Du baust unsere UGC-Maschine: Creator finden, briefen, Hooks schreiben, jede Woche 10–20 Ad-Varianten testen, lernen, wiederholen.

  • Du bringst 5.000 Familien auf die Warteliste, bevor es Onoo zu kaufen gibt – und hältst sie bei Laune (Newsletter, Social, „Kinderfrage des Tages“).

  • Du machst aus unseren Beta-Familien Fans: Reviews, Videos, Testimonials, echte Geschichten.

  • Du baust den Funnel von Warteliste bis Abo: Landingpage, Shop, E-Mail-Flows, Empfehlungsprogramm, Abo-Aktivierung, Kündigungs-Prävention.

  • Du schaltest Paid Social (Meta, TikTok) selbst, misst sauber (Tracking, Attribution, CAC, LTV) und entscheidest nach Zahlen.

  • Du bringst uns in die Magazine, Podcasts und Feeds, die Eltern in DACH wirklich lesen und hören.

  • Du machst die Gründer sichtbar (LinkedIn, Instagram) – vor dem Launch unser günstigster Kanal.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass unser Marketing hält, was das Produkt verspricht: keine Kinder als Werbefiguren, Datenschutz vorgelebt, Werbung sauber gekennzeichnet, kein Fake-UGC.

  • Du hast ein Krisen-Playbook in der Schublade, falls Onoo einem Kind mal etwas Falsches sagt.

  • Du baust ab dem Launch das Team und holst Freelancer und Agenturen dazu, wo es sich lohnt.

Melde dich, wenn:

  • Du 5+ Jahre Consumer-Marketing gemacht hast, am liebsten D2C mit Abo oder Hardware.

  • Du schon mal eine Marke von null aufgebaut hast oder beim Aufbau ganz vorne dabei warst.

  • Du UGC nicht nur kennst, sondern eine Creative-Testing-Maschine gebaut hast und uns sagen kannst, welche Hook-Rate dein bestes Creative hatte und warum.

  • Du Lifecycle-Marketing kannst: Klaviyo oder Ähnliches, Flows, Segmente, Churn.

  • Du Zahlen magst: CAC, LTV, Cohorts, Payback und mit unserem Finance-Mitgründer eine Sprache sprichst.

  • Du selbst Ads schaltest, Texte schreibst, Videos schneidest, Decks baust und nicht nur delegierst.

  • Du den DACH-Markt kennst und verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse mitbringst.

  • Du KI-Tools für Content täglich nutzt und weißt, wo ihre Grenze ist.

  • Du Kinder, Eltern und Bildung spannend findest. Nicht nur als Zielgruppe.

  • Du Verantwortung willst, bevor alles fertig ist.

Eher nicht, wenn: du zuletzt vor allem Budgets und Agenturen gesteuert hast und nicht mehr selbst Hand anlegen willst. Oder wenn du nur Performance kannst, aber keine Marke. Oder nur Marke, aber keine Zahlen.

data.title: Lead Cloud Engineer (m/w/d)
data.description:
Über das Unternehmen

Unser Partner Datasolut ist eine Data- & AI-Beratung aus Köln. Das Team hilft Unternehmen dabei, aus ihren Daten echten Mehrwert zu machen: von der ersten KI-Strategie über moderne Lakehouse-Plattformen bis hin zu Machine-Learning- und Agentic-AI-Lösungen, die im Alltag tatsächlich laufen. Und nicht nur auf Folien gut aussehen.

Was Datasolut macht:Datasolut begleitet seine Kunden auf dem ganzen Weg: gemeinsam verstehen, wo sie stehen, umsetzen, was wirklich gebraucht wird, und skalieren, was funktioniert. Strategie und Umsetzung kommen aus einer Hand. Kein Übergeben, kein Neu-Erklären, kein Stille-Post-Spiel.Technologisch ist Datasolut ganz vorne mit dabei: Als Databricks Silver Partner und einer der wenigen Microsoft Fabric Featured Partner in Deutschland arbeitest du mit den Plattformen, die gerade die Datenwelt prägen. CTO Laurenz ist Databricks MVP. Heißt für dich: Hier lernst du von Leuten, die wissen, wovon sie reden.

So arbeitet das Team:Datasolut ist kein Konzern, und das ist auch gut so. Es gibt kurze Wege, flache Hierarchien und echte Verantwortung von Anfang an. Deine Ideen landen nicht in einer Schublade, sondern im nächsten Projekt. Das Team teilt Wissen, hilft sich gegenseitig weiter und feiert Erfolge gemeinsam.

Klingt nach dir? Dann bewirb dich! Wir freuen uns, dich kennenzulernen und dich mit Datasolut zusammenzubringen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du baust für unsere Kunden Cloud-Infrastrukturen und -Ressourcen in Microsoft Azure auf, verbindest Netzwerke und Datenquellen und bettest alles sauber in das Gesamtkonstrukt ein.

  • Du setzt Infrastructure as Code mit Terraform selbst um, inklusive Deployments, und sorgst mit CI/CD für saubere und robuste Prozesse.

  • Du führst das wachsende Cloud-Team mit aktuell drei Engineers fachlich.

  • Du baust Standards und Best Practices für die Cloud-Projekte auf, damit bei jedem Kunden schneller und verlässlicher geliefert wird.

  • Du entwickelst den Bereich Cloud weiter, bringst neue Impulse in unser Angebot ein und erkennst Potenziale bei unseren Kunden.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit unseren Data & AI Engineers zusammen, damit Cloud-Infrastruktur, Datenplattformen wie Databricks und KI-Lösungen nahtlos zusammenspielen.

Das bringst du mit

  • Ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.

  • 4 bis 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Cloud Engineering, idealerweise mit Schwerpunkt Microsoft Azure.

  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit Infrastructure as Code, insbesondere Terraform, sowie mit CI/CD und DevOps-Prinzipien.

  • Gutes Verständnis von Netzwerken, Security und der Anbindung von Datenquellen in Cloud-Umgebungen.

  • Erfahrung mit Databricks ist ein großes Plus. Kenntnisse in AWS oder Snowflake sind ebenfalls willkommen.

  • Beratungserfahrung ist sehr wünschenswert. Vor allem solltest du Bock auf Kundenkontakt haben.

  • Führungserfahrung ist kein Muss. Wichtig ist, dass du Lust hast, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und andere fachlich weiterzubringen.

  • Organisationstalent und Kommunikationsstärke: Du behältst den Überblick und erklärst komplexe Themen verständlich; im Team genauso wie gegenüber Nicht-Techies.

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (Muttersprache oder C1-Niveau mit Nachweis) und gute Englischkenntnisse.

Das bekommst du

  • Projekte mit echtem Impact statt Beschäftigungstherapie

  • Arbeiten mit modernsten Data- & AI-Technologien wie Databricks und Microsoft Fabric

  • Ein Team, das Bock auf Daten hat und dich mitzieht

  • Raum zum Lernen, Ausprobieren und Wachsen

  • Wahl zwischen JobRad und Deutschlandticket (Urban Sports Club folgt bald!)

  • 3 Tage Homeoffice pro Woche

  • Modernes Office mit zwei Büroflächen im Herzen von Köln-Ehrenfeld - viele Restaurants für die Mittagspause sind fußläufig erreichbar

  • Eigenes Gym im Office und alle 2 Wochen dienstags nach Feierabend Training mit unserer Personal Trainerin

Your opportunity:

AI is shifting how the best products get built. The handoffs between product, design, and engineering are slowing us down. The companies moving fastest are doing it with people who own the full loop, from the user problem to the shipped feature, without losing the thread.

At Taxfix, we’re rebuilding our R&D organization around this idea. We call these people builders.

A Builder has a primary craft, one they’re genuinely excellent at, but they don’t stop there. They stretch across product, design, and engineering as the situation demands, using AI to cover the gaps. They’re accountable to outcomes, not job descriptions.

Taxfix has put €5 billion back into our customers’ pockets and we aren’t stopping there. We operate in Germany, Spain, and the UK, and we’re in the middle of a genuine AI transformation in how we build and how we’re organized.

Assume there’s no designer to give you a Figma file. No engineer to hand the spec to. The magic is knowing what to build, why, and in what order, then making it happen. If building the thing sounds more natural to you than describing it, this role is for you.

 

Your responsibilities and decisions:

  • Take a user problem from rough idea to shipped product. Write the brief, design the flow, prototype it, and get it in front of users, with as few handoffs as possible. Own the full loop.

  • Compress research, synthesis, and spec-writing from weeks into hours. You reach for AI tools not because you’ve been asked to, but because they faster make you faster in delivering high quality outcome. You know when to trust the output, when to edit it, and when to reject it. Use AI as a force multiplier.

  • You structure fuzzy problems, identify what should and shouldn’t be built, and move forward when there are dozens of possible directions. The magic is in the trade-offs, not the feature list. Turn ambiguous ideas into things users can trust.

  • You collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders on AI-related product work, translating AI concepts, capabilities, limitations, and outputs into clear product decisions. You work effectively in hybrid human-AI teams. Work in small, focused teams.

  • You know the metric your team is trying to move. You measure your week by what changed in user behaviour, not by how many tickets moved to Done. Be accountable to outcomes, not roadmaps.

data.description:
At Upvest, we are on a mission to make investing as easy as spending money. Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business.

We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive. Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience.

About the role:

The Growth team at Upvest is driving our go-to-market activities, spanning across Marketing, Sales and Customer Success. Our mission is to become the Investment-as-a-service category leader for Europe's leading brokers, banks, wealth managers, and non-financial platforms. We're honoured to work with some of Europe's leading brands in a fast moving and expanding market already and are just getting started.

 

As Upvest enters the next stage of growth, we are seeking a highly motivated and outcome-driven Account Executive to join us. All our team efforts are centred around the client and give you the opportunity to work with high autonomy coupled with inspirational leadership. Working in the Growth team combines impactful work with a relaxed and fun atmosphere. We have established strong practices around feedback, team health and social events.

 

In this role, you will work directly with our Director Business Development DACH Sven Loeckel to drive our Financial Institutions sales - winning and delighting our clients and collaborating closely with our growth and launch teams to help large financial institutions to digitise their investing propositions. You’ll leverage your expertise in financial services and sales to understand our clients’ needs and craft a compelling commercial proposition for them. This is an opportunity to own sizeable client relationships and thus having a direct impact by both driving the Upvest business and transforming the retail investment market.

What you’ll do:

  • Own the cross-functional sales cycle until contract closing to meet or exceed sales targets

  • Build the business by consultatively understanding our clients’ needs and developing compelling sales materials that communicate the Upvest value proposition effectively

  • Contribute to our sales enablement efforts and process improvement by sharing client insights and driving best practice

  • Enable a seamless client onboarding experience via effective communication with our implementations team

What you bring:

  • Experience: You have 3 – 6 years of experience in sales-related roles, ideally within investments, banking, or wealth management, preferably in a B2B environment and working with API-based products. Alternatively, you have 4–6+ years of experience at a specialised financial services consultancy, working on IT infrastructure-related projects, ideally within the investment services space

  • Industry Exposure: You have previous experience in investments and securities trading, along with a strong interest in software- and infrastructure-as-a-service products (e.g. BaaS)

  • Client-centric sales: You have demonstrated expertise with B2B sales methodologies, such as solution/consultative selling as well as practical application of industry best practices, always starting with the clients needs’

  • Stakeholder management Skills: You have demonstrated strong leadership skills, are able to communicate well with different stakeholder groups, and are not afraid to challenge assumptions internally or externally

  • Negotiation Skills: Strong relationship-building and negotiation skills, with the ability to create trust, effectively handle objections and present compelling pitches

  • Project Management: Hands-on, proactive ownership of complex projects, including ensuring consistent and reliable communication with multiple client and internal stakeholders and diligent internal documentation

It’s great if you have:

  • Experience selling to banks or wealth managers

  • Industry Knowledge - thorough understanding of the investment industry, its current trends and competitive landscape

  • Professional Network: Strong professional network in the investment industry

  • Location Preference: Preference for candidates located in Berlin / remote Germany and fluent in German (C2 or native)

How we Upvest in you:

  • Best-in-class AI tools: Every Upvenger has €20,000 per year to spend on the best AI tools available — so you're always working with the most powerful models and tooling on the market.

  • Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits.

  • Wellbeing: Recharge with 30 days of annual leave and maintain a healthy lifestyle with sports benefits. Access confidential professional coaching and enjoy the flexibility to work remotely abroad for up to 183 days a year. Recharge with UpRest, a one-month fully paid sabbatical after every 4 years of working at Upvest.

We enable anyone to be an investor. Our mission is to grow investing opportunities for all European customers and businesses. By empowering FinTechs, banks, and wealth managers to offer investment products, we help create financial well-being for their customers.

lemon.markets is a Brokerage-as-a-Service platform: simple digital access to capital markets through a single API. By combining dwpbank’s long-standing expertise and stability with lemon.markets’ technology-first mindset and speed, we are building a modern, modular securities services ecosystem. Together, we offer faster time-to-market, modular services, and a modern customer experience that helps financial service providers stay competitive and respond more flexibly in a changing market.

Your Mission

As an Associate Product Manager in the Customer Lifecycle domain, you will support the engine which makes sure our already onboarded customers have a positive experience on lifecycle events like re-KYC, account termination and customer service. Furthermore, you will be responsible for making sure lemon.markets delivers on its ongoing regulatory commitments. Your remit also covers owning the tooling which our operations colleagues use every day and making sure these evolve in sync with evolving regulatory landscape as well as business growth.

Reporting to the domain's Senior PM, you'll drive complex, multi-stakeholder commitments end-to-end. You'll work cross-functionally at lemon.markets and regularly interface with stakeholders from varying functional backgrounds. To be successful in this role, you should be able to bring stakeholders on the same page and drive a coherent product strategy aimed at improving the efficiency of processes which kick-in during the lifecycle of a customer with lemon.markets while making sure lemon.markets adheres to its regulatory obligations.

In this role you will:

  • Own the roadmap for the problem space end-to-end - i.e. from problem framing through to release, adoption and iteration.

  • Be embedded in a cross-functional team including operations and engineering, while engaging with other product teams, solutions engineering, and your colleagues in functions such as finance, risk and compliance.

  • Prioritise commitments against the domain strategy using quantitative and qualitative evidence, and share your trade-offs.

  • Propose forward-looking solutions that outlive the immediate ask, rather than one-off tactical fixes.

  • Interface regularly with your immediate customers and stakeholders to understand their pain points, capture feedback and use this information to shape your roadmap and product strategy.

  • Track market and regulatory developments in your problem space, and bring the insights back to the team and introduce informed iterations of your product strategy.

  • Write clearly and often - decision records, partner-facing specs, internal narratives. Writing is how decisions get made here.

You’ll be successful in this role if:

  • You have at least 1-2 years of product experience, including independently shipping complex products. You take ownership of outcomes, not just features.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity. You can define an unclear problem space, structure it, and move forward without waiting for someone to hand you a spec.

  • You are comfortable working through legal text. You form your own preliminary view on a legal or regulatory question before discussing it with experts, and you know which questions to bring to them.

  • You argue your position based on data and evidence, and you iterate when the evidence changes.

  • You write clearly. Decisions, specs, and partner communication are a core part of this job, and you can make complex topics easy to follow on paper.

  • You use AI tools in your day-to-day work and actively explore how far they can take your output.

  • You are professionally fluent in English. However, German speakers would be preferred.

How we take care of you:

  • 🚀 Compensation package: We offer you a competitive salary, based on your experience and the value-add you bring to lemon.markets.

  • 🕑 Flexible working hours: We trust people to choose when they work best and avoid a rigid 9 to 5 mindset. You decide on the rhythm that helps you do your best work, with only shared core hours from 12:00 to 16:00 to support collaboration.

  • 🏢 Hybrid work setup: You can work from anywhere in Germany within a hybrid model. At the same time, in-person collaboration is a key part of our culture. That being said, individual contributor lemoneers work 4 or more days per month on-site in our Berlin office, spending quality time together with the team at events, onsites/offsites or over team dinners.

  • 📈 Grow with us: We take your personal development seriously! You’ll get regular mentorship and stretch opportunities, a clear career development framework with frequent feedback conversations as well as an annual learning budget.

  • 🌱 People & culture: You’ll feel our culture in the small things, like Polaroids from our lemoneers’ first day and our monthly new-joiner breakfasts. But also in the bigger things, like celebrating the onboarding of new partners or our annual offsites, where the whole company comes together to connect, reflect, and celebrate.

  • 💛 Perks & benefits: We choose benefits that add actual value. We sponsor a Deutschlandticket for employees on unlimited contracts, plus 50% off on Beatvest - our partner for financial education and investing.

  • 🏝 Workation: Get out of here! At lemon.markets you can work remotely from anywhere in the EU for up to 10 consecutive days at a time, and up to 60 days per year in total.

As an equal opportunity employer, lemon.markets is committed to building an inclusive workplace. The company welcomes people from all different backgrounds, including age, citizenship, ethnic and racial origins, gender identities, individuals with disabilities, marital status, religions and ideologies, and sexual orientations to apply.

If you feel this role could be a great match for you even if you don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you, please apply.

data.description:

Als GTM-Intern (m/f/d) bist du für das vordere Ende unserer M&A-Maschine verantwortlich. Jede Hausverwaltung in Deutschland ist ein potenzielles Übernahmeziel. Dein Job ist es, sie zu finden, sie zu erreichen und einen Austausch zu starten.

Warum jetzt einsteigen

  • Wir wachsen schnell mit einem kleinen, eng vernetzten Team: In den letzten 3 Jahren sind wir mit rund 20 Vollzeitkräften zur zweitgrößten Hausverwaltung Deutschlands geworden.

data.title: GTM (DACH)
data.description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

We are looking for an enthusiastic, driven, and proactive commercial analyst to join our expanding DACH go-to-market team. As a key member of our commercial team, you will play a crucial role in sourcing and qualifying leads, initiating outreach, and scheduling high-value conversations for our Account Executives. Your goal will be to create meaningful connections with healthcare practices and hospital groups, facilitating our mission to win across the DACH market.

This role requires a proactive mindset, excellent communication skills, and the ability to thrive in a high-growth startup environment. You will become an expert in engaging healthcare stakeholders, driving new opportunities, and contributing directly to the sales pipeline.

What you’ll do

  • Identify, research, and prospect potential customers and formulate go-to-market strategies

  • Execute inbound and outbound campaigns using a mix of calls, emails, social selling, and product-led signals to qualify leads.

  • Schedule high-quality meetings and product demonstrations for Account Executives, ensuring smooth handoff of qualified opportunities.

  • Own and manage end-to-end sales cycles for small SMB customers, from initial outreach through to closing deals.

  • Maintain accurate records in HubSpot CRM, manage and optimise sales pipelines, and consistently meet targets for qualified leads generated.

  • Collaborate closely with Account Executives, Marketing, Product, Operations, and Customer Success teams to streamline sales strategies and market positioning.

  • Stay updated on market trends, competitor activities, and evolving customer needs to identify new opportunities.

What we're looking for

  • 1-2 years of experience in sales or in tech, banking, consulting, PE/VC or similar.

  • Proven success in generating leads, qualifying prospects, and managing high-volume outreach campaigns.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, able to quickly build rapport and articulate the value of Heidi’s AI-driven healthcare solutions.

  • Highly organised, disciplined, and results-oriented with a strong problem-solving ability and the ability to prioritise multiple tasks simultaneously.

  • Comfortable working independently in a dynamic, fast-paced startup environment with a high degree of accountability.

  • Eager to learn, adaptable, and excited about professional growth opportunities.

Attitude is more important than experience so if you are a hungry, competitive and highly motivated operator who has a knack for problem solving and building relationships we want to hear from you.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

data.title: C005419 Senior Project Transition Manager (NS) - FRI 13 Nov RELAUNCH
data.description:
Deadline Date: Friday 13 November 2026

Requirement: Senior Project Transition Manager

Location: Wiesbaden, DE

Full Time On-Site: Yes

Time On-Site: 100%

Total Scope of the request (hours): 350

Required Start Date: 7 December 2026

End Contract Date: 31 December 2026

Required Security Clearance: NATO SECRET

 

Duties & Role: 

Project Transition to Operations

  • Leads the transition of projects and capabilities into operational service, from early engagement in project planning through to formal handover and early life support.
  • Defines and agrees transition plans, entry and exit criteria, service acceptance criteria and handover deliverables with Project Managers, Service Owners and customers.
  • Ensures operational readiness prior to go-live: support model, staffing, training, documentation, spares, underpinning contracts, monitoring and configuration data are in place.
  • Evaluates project outputs against agreed service acceptance criteria and formally recommends acceptance, conditional acceptance or rejection.
  • Identifies, manages and escalates transition risks, issues and dependencies, and ensures residual risks are understood and owned by operations.
  • Manages early life support and closes transition only when agreed service performance has been demonstrated.
  • Captures and applies lessons identified to improve future transitions.

Local Operations Management (Wiesbaden)

  • Takes accountability for the day-to-day delivery of NCIA services at the location, including service performance, customer satisfaction and compliance with security and safety requirements.
  • Leads and coordinates local technical, support and contractor personnel, setting clear priorities, standards and direction.
  • Oversees the local infrastructure (facilities, networks, data centre / server rooms, end-user and deployable CIS assets) and ensures it is maintained, secured and fit for purpose.
  • Ensures asset and configuration management records for the location are accurate and complete.
  • Coordinates local business continuity and service recovery arrangements.

Incident and Problem Management

  • Ensures incidents are logged, prioritised, diagnosed and resolved according to agreed procedures and service levels.
  • Leads the resolution of major incidents, coordinating technical teams, vendors and customers, and provides timely, accurate communication to senior stakeholders.
  • Escalates unresolved incidents and facilitates recovery following resolution.
  • Initiates and monitors problem investigations, drives root cause analysis and ensures preventive measures are implemented.
  • Analyses incident and problem trends to reduce recurrence and improve service stability.

Change Management

  • Manages the change control process for services and assets at the location and for services in transition.
  • Assesses changes for risk, impact, cost and resource requirements, and represents the location in Change Advisory Boards.
  • Ensures changes are planned, communicated, tested, implemented and reviewed in a controlled manner, minimizing disruption to operations.

Service Level Management

  • Negotiates service level requirements and agreed service levels with customers, and contributes to Service Level Agreements, Operational Level Agreements and underpinning contracts.
  • Monitors service performance and key performance indicators, diagnoses service delivery problems and initiates improvement actions.
  • Provides accurate and regular performance reporting to NCIA management and customers.
  • Drives continual service improvement across processes, tools and third-party delivery.

Cost, Resource and Vendor Management

  • Manages the operational and transition budget for the location, including cost planning, forecasting, tracking and variance reporting.
  • Provides inputs to customer budget processes, cost models and service rates, ensuring the full cost of operating transitioned services is identified and funded.
  • Identifies cost optimisation opportunities without compromising service levels or security.
  • Manages vendor and contractor performance against contractual obligations, statements of work and service levels, and supports procurement activities as required.

 

Specific Working Conditions: Occasional travel within NATO nations, including to operational sites, may be required.

Requirements

Skills, Knowledge & Experience:

  • The candidate must have a currently active NATO SECRET security clearance
  • A minimum requirement of a Bachelor's degree at a nationally recognised/certified university in Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration or a related discipline, and 8 years' post-related experience.
  • Or exceptionally, the lack of a university degree may be compensated by the demonstration of a candidate's particular abilities or experience that is/are of interest to the NCI Agency, that is, at least 12 years' extensive and progressive expertise in duties related to the function of the post.
  • Minimum 8 years of combined experience in IT service management and project management, of which at least 3 years in a senior role.
  • Proven experience (minimum 5 years) in IT service management in a Service Delivery Manager, IT Operations Manager or similar role, including incident, problem, change and service level management.
  • Proven experience (minimum 5 years) in project management, delivering complex IT/CIS projects to time, cost and quality.
  • Demonstrable track record of transitioning projects or new capabilities into live operational service.
  • Proven experience engaging, influencing and briefing senior stakeholders at executive (C-level) or General/Flag Officer level.
  • Experience managing IT infrastructure (networks, data centres, servers, end-user and communications systems) in an operational environment.
  • Experience in budget and cost management, including forecasting, cost control and financial reporting.
  • Proven experience managing vendors and contractors against contractual and service level obligations.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams in an international environment.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.

data.title: Outbound Field Account Executive - EMEA
Engineering Lead
data.description:
You'll ship agents that move money, and you'll keep the rhythm that gets them shipped. Accounts payable, accounts receivable, treasury: autonomous agents that read the invoice, match it, negotiate the discount, release the payment, and reconcile the cash. Every one of those actions runs in production with a customer's CFO watching the result.

Most of what the industry calls engineering culture was written for a world where humans typed every line. That world ended. We want to build the 2026 version: engineers who work with agents as a matter of course, where the unit of work is the loop (spec, generate, evaluate, correct, ship) rather than the ticket, where code review means reviewing the evals and prompts as hard as the diff, and where a regression suite over real customer invoices is what lets us move fast on systems that touch money. Nobody has a settled playbook for this. You'll help write ours, from inside a pod.

This is a player-coach role. You'll spend most of your week shipping code in one of our pods, and you'll manage the engineers day to day: 1:1s, feedback, growth, the hard conversation when it's needed. The rest goes to the delivery rhythm: pods commit to milestones in Linear, post progress daily, and review misses every Friday with the Head of Product and the CTO. You run that review and the follow-ups. The management share grows as we go from 8 engineers to 16 and beyond; this role is the natural path to Head of Engineering. You'll report to the CTO. Causa Prima is built by the team behind Taulia and backed by Creandum.

What you'll do

  • Ship as a senior engineer, 70 to 80% of your week. Take the hardest work in your pod, unblock the integration nobody wants, and review the code that touches money personally. You set the bar by clearing it in front of the team.

  • Manage the engineers day to day. Weekly 1:1s, direct feedback, growth plans, and the honest conversation about who's ready for more scope and who's in the wrong seat. The CTO owns hiring decisions and the technical direction; the people in the pods are yours.

  • Run the delivery rhythm. Weekly milestone commitments, the Friday review, the dashboard of committed versus delivered, and the follow-ups when something slips. Misses are discussed to learn, not to blame; your job is that they get discussed at all, with an owner and a next step.

  • Make the loop the way we work. Specs written so an agent can execute them, evals that run before merge, review practices that treat prompts as code. The CTO owns the architecture; you own that every pod actually works this way, including the change management when they don't.

  • Raise risk early. You know on Tuesday what won't make Friday, and so does everyone who needs to.

  • Sit with customers. Controllers explaining why the agent's match was technically correct and operationally wrong. AP leads walking you through an SAP extension nobody documented. That's where the next milestone comes from.

What we're looking for

  • A senior engineer who likes the operational side. You've shipped production systems where mistakes cost money: fintech, payments, ERP-adjacent, enterprise B2B. You've also managed engineers, run their 1:1s and a delivery cadence, and liked it enough to want more of it while still writing code.

  • You build with agents. You've shipped something in the last month using an agentic coding tool that saved you a week, and you can show us. Python or TypeScript in anger, and enough PostgreSQL to review a migration without asking.

  • You've kept commitments reliable before, with numbers. Committed versus shipped, cycle time, whatever you tracked. You've followed up on slipped work without it turning into a blame exercise.

  • Minimal process instincts. You add a ritual when it earns its place and remove it when it doesn't. A weekly review that takes 30 minutes, not 90.

  • You can disagree with a founder and stay in the room. We hire for trust and challenge in that order.

  • Fluent English. German or Spanish is a plus. Munich preferred, Madrid works. You'll be in both offices regularly.

This is a wishlist, not a checklist. If the role excites you but you don't tick every box, we would encourage you to apply anyway.

Nice to have

  • AI agents in production, as the product rather than a feature.

  • Depth in purchase-to-pay or order-to-cash, or scar tissue from an SAP integration.

  • You've grown with a team through a Series A or B.

  • Former founder or founding engineer.

data.title: Staff Engineer
data.description:
Staff Engineer

You'll be the most senior engineer on the agents that run finance operations for our customers — designing, building, and operating the autonomous agents that handle accounts payable and receivable end-to-end. From invoice validation and dispute resolution to cross-company negotiation and cash optimization.

This is an individual-contributor role at the top of our ladder: no direct reports, full technical authority over the architecture the rest of the team builds on.

What you'll do

  • Agent architecture — Design the multi-agent system: agent boundaries, event contracts, orchestration patterns, and the separation between LLM reasoning and deterministic enforcement. LLMs inform; rules enforce. You own where that line sits for every action that moves money, and the authorization gateway that makes it non-negotiable.

  • Agentic dispute resolution — An agent that reads the claim, gathers the evidence from the PO, contract, and delivery record, forms a position, and works it to settlement — negotiating with the counterparty where that's appropriate, escalating to a human where it isn't. Deductions and short pays classified, tied to the underlying claim, and driven to resolution rather than parked in an aging bucket.

  • Agentic dynamic discounting — Agents that continuously price early payment against the cash position on both sides of the transaction, propose terms, and execute them. Static payment terms become a negotiation that runs on its own.

  • Matching and reconciliation — Three-way matching across purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice with configurable tolerances; cash application against bank statements and remittance advices, including partial payments and residuals; the exception paths that follow when any of it fails. Unglamorous but important: The foundation everything agentic sits on.

  • Validation & anomaly detection — Business rule checks, duplicate and near-duplicate detection, pricing discrepancy detection, and anomaly detection across time. Precision matters as much as recall here: a false positive is a blocked supplier and an angry procurement lead.

  • Integration framework — ERP systems first and deepest, then banking APIs, accounting platforms, Gmail, Drive, and Slack. Auth model, credential lifecycle, data normalization. Today each connector is a project; you make the next one a configuration.

  • Compliance & security — Agents operate within a zero-trust model. You'll design how agents verify independently against source data, how outbound content is reviewed, and how the system prevents cascading failures from prompt injection. Plus the European e-invoicing mandates now landing across France, Germany, and Spain, and what EN 16931 means for the pipeline.

  • Platform & data infrastructure — Own the primitives every agent action rests on: an append-only PostgreSQL event store with tamper-evident hash chaining for replay and audit; cryptographic signature verification on agent events and approval chains before anything external fires; the Workflow Constraint Engine that gates payments, emails, and API calls on deterministic policy, not model output; row-level multi-tenancy and tenant-scoped credentials across every data store; attribute-based authorization via Cerbos, evaluated the same way whether the caller is an agent or a human; and the MCP security layer — auth, capability-scoping, rate limiting — for external agent-to-agent access.

  • The engineering standard — Architecture decision records, review bar, on-call, and a clear view of what we deliberately don't build. You'll write the things the next ten engineers read in week one, and you'll spend time with controllers and AP leads watching agents fail in ways no test predicted.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years shipping production systems; currently Staff, Principal, Lead IC, or a founding engineer. You've carried an architecture through a scaling step and lived with your own decisions.

  • Strong systems design thinking — agent boundaries, failure modes, trust boundaries, contract evolution. Money movement is not retry-safe by default and you already know why.

  • Depth in Python and/or TypeScript in production, and deep PostgreSQL: event sourcing, row-level security, indexing tradeoffs, schema evolution under load.

  • Hands-on experience with LLM-powered systems, agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, or similar), and document AI (LlamaIndex, LlamaParse, or similar).

  • Strong opinions about when to use an LLM vs. a rules engine vs. traditional ML — and the courage to defend them.

  • Experience designing data pipelines, integration architectures, or event-driven systems in production.

  • Security awareness — you think about what happens when untrusted input meets your pipeline, and about segregation of duties before someone makes you.

  • Technical leadership without a title: reviews that teach, designs that get adopted, engineers who get faster because you're there.

  • Effective use of AI coding tools with strong review skills for LLM integration and auth code.

  • Domain knowledge across the purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash cycle. You don't need all three areas below, but you need real depth in one and working fluency in the rest — enough that when a controller describes an exception, you understand it before they finish:

    • Accounts payable — PO and non-PO invoice intake, coding to GL account and cost centre, approval routing and delegation of authority, three-way matching and tolerance handling, blocked-invoice and exception workflows, duplicate detection, payment runs, payment terms and early-payment discounts, supplier master data and bank-detail verification, period-end accruals for un-invoiced receipts.

    • Accounts receivable — invoice issuance and e-invoicing, cash application and remittance matching, partial payments, short pays and residuals, credit memos, deductions and dispute handling, dunning and collections strategy, credit limits and credit risk, aging and DSO.

    • Procurement — requisition to purchase order, supplier onboarding and qualification, catalogues and contract pricing, goods receipt, off-contract and maverick spend, sourcing and supplier negotiation, and the handoff into AP where most of the pain actually lives.

  • Fluency with the systems this runs on: ERPs (NetSuite, Dynamics, or the SMB stack), the sub-ledger to general-ledger relationship, and how period close constrains what an agent is allowed to do and when.

Nice to have:

  • Peppol and EN 16931 in production, or bank connectivity via ISO 20022.

  • Cryptographic primitives in production: digital signatures, hash chaining, tamper-evident logs.

  • SOC 2, GDPR, or data-residency engineering in a regulated environment.

  • You've founded something, or have been employee 1 to 5 in a startup.

About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

What you will own

• Roadmap and backlog: own the SF backlog end to end. Run intake across Sales, Operations, Finance, and Customer Success and translate business needs into clear requirements with acceptance criteria and priority.

• Automation delivery: design, build, and test declarative automation (Flow, validation rules, approval processes, assignment logic) but also manage the AI layer accross the org.

• Developer partnership: scope Apex-heavy and integration work with our Salesforce developers, review their output for fit and maintainability, and decide what belongs in configuration versus code.

• Administration and operations: own day-to-day administration: users and licenses, the security and sharing model, profiles and permission sets, sandbox and release management, and business-as-usual support. This is the Administrator function.

• Data quality and governance: protect the integrity of the data model, prevent one-off requests from fragmenting it, and own deduplication, validation, and reporting hygiene.

• Stakeholder management: be the single point of contact for everything Salesforce. Set expectations, communicate tradeoffs, and report progress against the automation targets.

What you bring

• 5+ years on the Salesforce platform, with real ownership of an org's roadmap or backlog

• Expert in declarative automation: Flow, validation rules, approval processes, and the security model

• Hands-on with day-to-day administration: users and licenses, profiles and permission sets, sandboxes, and release management

• Able to read and scope Apex, comfortable reviewing developer work and drawing the configuration-versus-code line

• A proven record of translating business needs into shipped solutions across multiple departments

• Salesforce Administrator certification; Advanced Administrator or Platform App Builder strongly preferred

• Fluent English, and comfort being the single owner of a business-critical system

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic. We believe that diversity drives innovation, creativity, and collective strength.

data.title: Generalist (Operations)
data.description:
Take on the business and back-end operations that keep Kairos running: finances, payments, HR, compliance, and systems, plus support for our programs and Pathfinder groups.

Note: This role description is a first draft. Scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve as our plans develop over the coming weeks, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

 

About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from METR, Redwood Research, AI Futures Project, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

We’re looking for a Generalist (Operations) to do the wide range of things that keep Kairos running in the background. The bulk of the role is core business and back-end operations: paying vendors, supervising accountants, supporting bookkeeping and our audit, figuring out how to employ and onboard people, and keeping us compliant. Alongside that, you’ll support our Pathfinder groups, process grants, build internal systems and automations, and pitch in on program ops.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Build systems and automations. Spot the operational work that shouldn’t be done by hand and automate it, so you and the team can spend time on the things that actually need judgment.

  • Run our finances and back-end operations. Pay vendors and contractors, supervise accountants, support bookkeeping and our annual audit, handle the logistics of employing people (payroll, benefits, onboarding and offboarding), and help keep us compliant. You won’t need to be an expert on day one, but you’ll learn to own these functions.

  • Process grants and payments. Run grant processing across Pathfinder and our other programs, make payments to individuals and organizations, and manage expense processing.

  • Pitch in on program ops and whatever else needs doing. Inbox triage, problem-solving on program logistics, and the occasional program-ops crunch where we need the hands.

 

Who You Are

  • Smart, agentic, and able to figure things out. A lot of this role is picking up unfamiliar processes (a new accounting task, a compliance requirement, a group’s odd request) and just working out how to do them well. We care about this more than about specific prior experience.

  • Great at automation and tooling. You instinctively reach for a better system rather than resigning yourself to doing things by hand, and you use AI and automation tools to get more done, complementing rather than replacing your own judgment. The best person in this role makes much of the repetitive work disappear.

  • Eager to help, and able to be assertive. You like unblocking people and improving their experience. You can be gentle but honest with a rejected applicant, and politely firm with an overly demanding one.

  • Organized and on top of things. You keep careful track of to-dos and information. When you drop a ball, it’s on purpose.

  • Strong writer and communicator. You’re clear and concise, and you think through your messaging from the reader’s perspective.

  • Mission-aligned. You care about making advanced AI go well, and you’re comfortable operating in the AI safety ecosystem and its culture.

While not required, we especially value:

  • Some experience in finance, accounting, HR, nonprofit compliance, event planning, or other business operations or nonprofit administration (but we’re glad to have you learn these on the job)

  • Strong automation and AI-tooling chops

  • Context on AI safety and the broader ecosystem

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The programs you’ll support influence hundreds of future AI safety and policy professionals.

  • Few ops roles are this broad. You’ll touch grants, finance, compliance, systems, and programs, and build unusually wide operating experience fast.

  • You’ll get to shape the role around your interests, with a say in which skills you build and which functions you take on.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

  • Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.

 

What We Offer

  • Base salary: $95,000–$190,000, depending on experience and location, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: Access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston; optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying

  • Remote, with expected travel 3-6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, though we have a light preference for people to work out of Berkeley.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • We may be able to provide visa sponsorship to the US, depending on the circumstances (especially, but not exclusively, O-1As).

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Screening call (15 mins)

  3. Take-home assignment (1.5–3 hours, paid)

  4. Interview (45 mins)

  5. Reference checks

  6. Work trial (3–4 days, paid - this can be flexibly scheduled around your other commitments)

  7. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

 

Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes 6 months with us, we’ll pay you a $5,000 referral bonus. Learn more here.

Compensation: $95K – $190K

About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join Motorway's Product & Engineering team. Motorway is a UK online car-selling platform connecting private sellers with ~7,500 verified dealers through online auctions. You will own a problem area end to end, in either the seller or the dealer side of the marketplace, and be accountable for the outcomes you deliver.

Building is cheaper than it has ever been. The hard part now is choosing the right thing to build. We want PMs with exceptional product sense who find the problems worth solving, back that judgement with evidence, and use the latest technology to solve them in ways that weren't possible a year ago.

What you will do

Find the problems that matter

  • Identify the highest-impact problem areas by combining quantitative analysis with qualitative research, and explain clearly why they matter more than the alternatives

  • See through the hundreds of good ideas to the few that will move the business and create real value for sellers and dealers

  • Own outcome-based goals and metrics, not feature lists

Build with AI, in your work and in our product

  • Use AI to make yourself and your team faster: automate routine PM tasks, analyse data and research quickly, and prototype or vibe code solutions to get customer feedback in days, not weeks

  • Ask how each product could be built differently given what AI makes possible, and bring those ideas to your squad

  • Make your team 2x more effective, not 2x busier

Deliver with rigour

  • Lead a cross-functional squad of engineers, designers and data specialists from discovery through launch and measurement

  • Run experiments that produce learning even when they fail, and act on what you learn

  • Make clear trade-offs between customer needs, technical constraints and business priorities

Bring people with you

  • Communicate the what, the why and the how clearly, through crisp, data-led documents and conversations

  • Work with the people closest to you (engineering, design, data) and with execs and other business units such as Operations, Customer Support, Sales and Marketing

  • Influence without authority and build alignment on difficult decisions

Requirements

  • Proven experience as a product manager, with a track record of shipping products that moved meaningful business metrics, not just delivering features

  • Strong product sense. You can show how you found and prioritised the right problem, and what you chose not to do

  • Comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative evidence: you run user research and also query data, design experiments and interpret results yourself

  • Data-oriented. You use data to understand problems, set goals and measure impact, and can debate approaches with data scientists and analysts

  • AI-forward. You use AI tools regularly in your own work and have hands-on experience prototyping or building with them. You have a point of view on where AI helps and where it doesn't

  • A clear, confident communicator who can work with engineers and analysts day to day and with senior leaders across the business

  • Ability to move between detail and strategy without losing coherence

  • Self-starter with strong ownership, a curious mindset, and the ability to build domain knowledge quickly

  • Experience in marketplaces, consumer products or B2B platforms is helpful but not essential

  • You're excited about changing how people buy and sell cars

Benefits

We offer a fantastic range of benefits to help you thrive:

  • Hybrid work schedule with 2 days per week in our Central London office, with regular social events, office drinks and free snacks to keep you going

  • Great work-life balance

  • Stock options so you can share in Motorway's growth and future success

  • Pension scheme to plan for your future with our provider NEST

  • Strong commitment to your personal development including budget for books, courses, conferences, etc

  • Opt-in comprehensive health insurance through BUPA including dental care and fitness discounts

  • Cycle to work scheme, save big ££ on a new bike and accessories

  • One paid volunteering day a year for you to use as you wish

  • Generous parental benefits including 6 months full paid maternity leave, 4 weeks paternity leave and workplace nursery scheme... and much more!

🌍 Fully distributed: Work remotely with diverse teams across UK, Europe, and Africa

What You'll Do

At M-KOPA, you'll build and operate distributed C# and .NET microservices on Azure, working within an event-driven architecture at significant scale. This is an outcomes-driven role: we care far more about the value you create than where you sit or how many hours you're online. You'll own what you build end-to-end — from idea, through implementation and deployment, into production and iteration.

Technical Environment 💻

  • Modern C# stack: Distributed C# and .NET microservices

  • Cloud & orchestration: Hosted on Azure using Kubernetes

  • Architecture: Event-driven, supporting products used at significant scale

  • Observability: Grafana, Azure Application Insights, logs, traces, and metrics

  • AI tooling: Claude and other AI tools used throughout the engineering workflow — design exploration, code generation and review, test writing, incident investigation, and technical communication

Our Engineering Approach 🚀

  • AI-native engineering: We want engineers who tinker — experimenting with new tools, agents, and workflows, and sharing what works

  • Guardrails as we accelerate: Automated tests, SLOs, alerting, observability, and deployment safeguards around everything we ship

  • On-call as feedback, not heroics: Engineers who build our systems also help operate them, using incidents to make the platform more resilient

What You Need

We're looking for a senior engineer who's curious, autonomous, and highly trusted. You're comfortable owning the entire software stack — including supporting infrastructure — throughout its lifecycle, and you see production data, not just deployment, as the real measure of "done."

  • Professional development programs and coaching partnerships

  • Family-friendly policies and flexible working arrangements

  • Well-being support and career growth opportunities

We create financial inclusion for the traditionally excluded through a fair, flexible, customer-centric financing model. We strive to drive greater inclusion of women, youth, and low-income communities.

Our Impact 💚

Our technology has created measurable change:

  • Connected 📱: 2.5 million first-time smartphone users connected

  • Prosperous 💰: 70% of customers use M-KOPA products for income generation, with 35,000 livelihoods created for agents

  • Green 🌱: 2.155 million tonnes of CO₂ avoided since 2010 through clean energy, refurbished devices, and e-mobility

Ready to build C#/.NET systems — with AI as part of your craft — that create real-world financial inclusion? Apply Now!

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com.

M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships. 

M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process.
