data.description:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Infrastructure Engineering and Tooling Team 👋

The Infrastructure Engineering and Tooling team, also known as Atlas, owns the ecosystem we use to deploy, run and manage services across the Trainline platform. Our work helps engineering teams across the business ship changes safely and confidently, so millions of travellers can rely on Trainline every day.

You'll join a collaborative team of software and platform engineers at all levels of experience. We work across Terraform, AWS, Node.js, C# and Python, and we don't expect you to know it all from day one. You'll work closely with engineers, Tech Leads and Engineering Managers, with support from a Senior Principal Engineer and the Head of Engineering, to improve our platform and deliver meaningful infrastructure change.

In this role as the Platform Engineer, you will...🚄

  • Contribute to improvements across Trainline's engineering platforms, building scalable, reliable and secure infrastructure that supports teams across the business.

  • Implement infrastructure changes with Terraform, following existing module patterns and suggesting ideas to improve quality, maintainability and automation.

  • Apply least-privilege and secure-by-default principles across our AWS accounts, helping our infrastructure meet Trainline's standards for security and operational excellence.

  • Build and improve automation, services and tooling in Node.js or Python to make delivery faster, safer and more repeatable.

  • Learn and grow with your colleagues through code reviews, pairing and shared knowledge, giving and receiving constructive feedback along the way.

  • Work with Tech Leads, Delivery Managers and cross-functional colleagues to understand priorities, plan your work and manage dependencies.

  • Raise risks, blockers and questions early, helping the team keep delivery moving at a sustainable pace.

  • Test, validate and deploy infrastructure changes through CI/CD (continuous integration and continuous delivery) pipelines, making sure they are robust, well documented and ready for production.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • Professional experience as a software engineer, writing code in Python, Node.js, C# or a similar programming language.

  • An understanding of software engineering best practice, with a focus on writing clean, maintainable and testable code.

  • Experience with AWS services such as ECS, Lambda, CloudFront, IAM and S3, following operational and security best practice.

  • Experience delivering infrastructure with Terraform or another infrastructure as code tool.

  • An understanding of DevOps practices and CI/CD, for example using GitHub Actions.

  • Experience using AI tooling in your day-to-day work, for example for coding, code review, research and productivity.

  • A curious mindset and the ability to pick up new technologies quickly and apply them well.

More information:

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

  • 🤝  Travel Together - We're one team 

  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor! 

Compensation: £60K – £70K

data.title: Community Lead
data.description:
Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS

At Accurx, we’ve supported thousands of healthcare organisations to deliver care for over 60 million patients. We’re used by 98% of GP practices and in 68% of NHS Trusts - that’s over 200,000 NHS staff each week.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that slow everything down and leave patients waiting. We're changing that. We’re transforming how NHS staff triage and prioritise patient demand, cut the admin that eats into clinical time, and work as one team across the system.

We've spent eight years proving care doesn't always need to happen in an appointment. In the best triage practices today, 40% of patient demand is resolved without one. Now we're taking that model system-wide – using AI to automate the work that slows healthcare down, connecting every part of the NHS and building the platform on which the future of healthcare work gets done.

About the role

You’ll support and scale one of the most engaged clinical communities in the UK. Our users already talk to each other every day. They share what works, solve problems together and advocate for better ways of working. But those conversations are spread across WhatsApp groups and Facebook channels, with no platform or structure behind them. Our ambassador programme is also ready to be taken further.

As our Community Lead reporting to the Head of Marketing, you’ll shape how healthcare professionals connect, learn from one another and drive change across the NHS. You’ll turn organic momentum into a scalable community that measurably drives product adoption, peer-to-peer learning and brand trust.

The challenges you’ll take on

  • Building strategic and large-scale communities: Shaping and delivering the long-term vision for our primary and secondary care communities, with community playing a clear role in driving product adoption and brand advocacy, not just engagement. You'll be actively running community initiatives, as well as setting the strategic direction.

  • Turning unstructured clinical conversations into scalable content: Creating repeatable ways to transform high-volume community conversations into user-led content, learning assets and programmes, using strong storytelling to make Accurx's value clear and compelling across the market.

  • Scaling advocacy through ambassadors and peer influence: Owning and evolving our ambassador programme that enable clinicians to influence their peers authentically, and aligning it closely with product and marketing priorities.

  • Owning our community platform and programmes: Choosing and implementing the right long-term platform to bring our community together, and deciding when existing tools are “good enough”. You’ll help Accurx invest in the right processes and operating models for a growing, multi-product, multi-care-setting community.

You should apply if...

  • You have proven experience building and growing communities in the thousands, ideally in SaaS, tech or healthcare. This is essential for the role.

  • You've used community as a core driver of commercial growth, product adoption or brand advocacy, rather than it being primarily focused on support, account management or research.

  • You have a strong track record of designing, running or scaling ambassador programmes and super-user initiatives that drive peer-to-peer learning and influence.

  • You can point to clear examples of turning unstructured community conversations into scalable, user-led content, with strong written communication and storytelling skills.

  • You bring a data-informed and tool-savvy mindset, using signals, feedback and AI to scale insight capture and content without losing authenticity.

  • You're a strong cross-functional collaborator, comfortable partnering closely with Product, User Research, Implementation, Product Marketing and Events.

What's in it for you?

data.description:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.


🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

This is a product-builder role, not a ticket-taking one. You own a product surface end to end: you talk to the customer, form the idea, build it, ship it, measure it, and decide what happens next. The same person who understands the repairer writes the code. There is no handoff for product quality to leak through.

You'll build at the center of a multi-trillion-dollar industry that still runs on phone calls, spreadsheets, and tribal knowledge. Replacement parts is one of the largest physical markets on earth and one of the least digitised, and there is no established playbook to copy. Partly is creating the category.

Our moat is Interpreter, a domain-specific AI model that understands parts, vehicles, and the messy real-world relationships between them in ways general-purpose models cannot. It is what lets software finally make sense of a physical, offline industry, and it is the engine underneath everything you build.

And what you build is changing shape. We are not bolting AI onto old screens. We are creating genuinely new agentic experiences for a broad spectrum of users, from estimators and parts managers to accountants and suppliers, where people express intent and supervise outcomes while agents handle the mechanical work. Designing how that trust is earned, surface by surface, while each one still delivers value today, is the heart of the role.

You'll work at an inflection point in how software itself gets built. AI-assisted development has collapsed the distance between an idea and a working version of it. The builders we want already work this way: they prototype in an afternoon, put it in front of real customers within days, and read the signal themselves. We want someone who works like that now, or is visibly building toward it.

💻 What will you do

  • Build, not just specify. Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted and LLM-assisted tooling, fast, disposable, real. Treat the prototype as the hypothesis and put it in front of real customers before writing the spec. Ship production code, instrument it, and watch how it actually gets used.

  • Stay close to customers. Spend time where the work happens. Understand what estimators, parts managers, and others actually do, where they lose time, and what better would feel like. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.

  • Reconcile signal. Combine what you see with what the data says, and reconcile the two when they disagree. Turn that understanding straight into what you build next.

  • Own the outcome. Steer by your surface's metrics; adoption and value delivered are yours. Make the call on priority and explain the reasoning, especially when the answer is no. When something is broken, own it, diagnose it precisely, and fix it.

  • Make the trade-off. Weigh product impact against engineering effort in the same breath, and find the cheaper path to the same outcome.

  • Build the agentic experience. Move your surface from manual operation toward supervised delegation: capture intent, decide where the human stays in the loop, and earn trust step by step so users never lose the thread of a high-stakes job.

  • Hold the craft. The surface feels fast, clear, and considered. You push back when something does not feel right, even when it technically works.

  • Raise the bar. Pair with SW Engineers on the harder systems work behind your surface, and contribute beyond your boundary: shared components, product craft, and what excellent building looks like here as the team grows.

🥷 Your skills

Non-negotiables

  • You ship end to end: a track record of taking features from idea to production, code included, with clear accountability for whether they worked. Roughly 3+ years building and shipping software in production.

  • Genuine customer obsession: a real habit of spending time with users in their work context, with a track record of that depth driving what you build.

  • Product taste and craft: the bar is experiences that feel effortless to time-pressured, non-technical users across fragmented, high-stakes workflows. Functional is not the finish line.

  • A point of view on agentic product design: how an experience moves from manual operation to supervised delegation, and how automation earns user trust gradually rather than all at once.

  • You build rapid prototypes yourself, with AI-assisted tools as a first instinct for testing an idea.

  • Solid full-stack engineering with a frontend lean: production-quality code and sound fundamentals. Systems-specialist depth is not the point of the role.

  • Trade-off fluency: you weigh product impact against engineering effort and often find a cheaper route to the same result.

  • Strong analytical instinct: you define the metric, build the view, read it, and act, without waiting for a data team.

  • You operate well in ambiguity and autonomy, and shape the problem rather than waiting for a spec.

Strong signals we look for

  • Shipped AI-assisted or agent-driven features in production, particularly where the human stays in the loop.

  • Built for a multi-persona, operational, or workflow-heavy B2B product.

  • Founder background, or early employee at a startup that scaled materially.

  • You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.

Bonus

  • Domain knowledge in automotive, the parts aftermarket, repair, or insurance claims.

  • Marketplace or network experience, from the demand or supply side.

  • Rust, or genuine eagerness to learn it. It is part of our stack.

Please note: if you don't have all the skills or experience listed above but believe you could be outstanding in this role, please still consider applying. Many people count themselves out. We'd love the chance to learn more about you and why you're exceptional.

🪅Benefits

  • Competitive base salary + equity. We offer competitive salaries and generous equity options for all full-time employees, ensuring everyone shares in the financial upside when we win.

  • Annual global offsite in New Zealand. Travel with the rest of the UK and EU team as we gather and connect for 1-2 weeks at our product and engineering hub in Christchurch.

  • Parental leave: Primary caregivers receive 3 months of fully paid parental leave, plus a flexible return-to-work (four days on full pay for your first three months back).

  • Team lunches: Lunch provided daily (Monday to Friday) in the office

  • Flexible working hours: We have flexible working hours and default to working from the office.

  • Season openers & events: We host regular events, including quarterly "season openers" for our UK/EU team, monthly team catch-ups, and weekly happy hours.

  • Healthy body, healthy mind: Every team member gets a £750 annual wellness allowance on a Partly-branded card. Use on gym memberships, rock climbing, physio, massage, GP visits, prescriptions; anything that you or your family, need.

data.description:
Platform Operations Lead

Location: NYC Metro Area (NY/NJ/CT) – Hybrid · London – Hybrid · Remote (US ET)

Company Description

Tangible is a fast-growing, tech-enabled platform providing liquidity solutions to LPs and GPs in the private markets secondaries ecosystem. Our Liquidity Hub enables leading wealth management platforms and their advisors to run secondary sales for their clients, from listing and bidding through to closing, and we are expanding transaction execution through our own US broker-dealer. By combining deep sector expertise with modern infrastructure, we unlock liquidity across private equity, private credit, and real assets.

Role Overview

The Platform Operations Lead will own the operational lifecycle of transactions on Tangible's platform, from listing through to final execution. The role covers deal setup on the platform, preparation and launch of liquidity windows, support through bidding and award, and execution through closing, settlement and fee collection.

As transaction volumes and our partner network grow, the Platform Operations Lead will drive the continued development of our operating model, refining processes, standardising partner playbooks and shaping the platform tooling that supports scale.

This is a hands-on, client-facing role, combining day-to-day management of a live transaction pipeline with ongoing process improvement. The role works across European and US hours and requires strong overlap with both.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the operational lifecycle of transactions on the platform, from deal setup and listing through bidding, award, closing, settlement and fee collection.

  • Prepare and launch liquidity windows with Product and our partners, and onboard buyers across partner platforms.

  • Manage a pipeline of parallel transactions against partner timelines, coordinating documentation, KYC and fund administrator review through to settlement.

  • Act as an operational point of contact for partners, GPs, fund administrators, buyers, sellers and their advisors.

  • Ensure every transaction runs within our broker-dealer's compliance framework, with complete, audit-ready records.

  • Work with Finance to invoice and collect fees on completed transactions.

  • Develop and maintain SOPs, partner playbooks and operating metrics.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on requirements, testing and internal tooling, and apply AI tools to automate operational work.

Requirements

  • 4 to 7 years' experience in transaction operations, deal execution or fund operations in private markets.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and confidence working directly with clients and institutional counterparties.

  • A track record of managing multiple live transactions against fixed deadlines with a high degree of accuracy.

  • Experience designing and improving operational processes.

  • Familiarity with KYC/AML requirements.

  • Proficiency with workflow platforms, e-signature tools and structured trackers, and an interest in applying AI tools to operations.

  • Willingness to obtain FINRA qualifications (SIE, Series 63 and Series 82), with company support.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Understanding of the secondary transaction lifecycle, including LP interest transfers: purchase and sale agreements, transfer and subscription agreements, capital account statements, GP consent and fund administrator workflows.

  • Experience at a secondaries platform or advisor, wealth platform, placement agent, fund administrator or transfer agent.

  • Experience in US broker-dealer operations or compliance, or existing FINRA registrations.

  • Experience with auction or window-based secondary processes, or with feeder and evergreen funds held by individual investors.

  • Reporting or data skills (SQL, Metabase or advanced spreadsheets).

If you thrive in fast-paced environments and want to model the future of a global tech brand—this is the team for you.

We're looking for a Senior Manager to join our Finance & Strategy team. In this role, you'll play an integral part in building our business strategy, ensuring we make the most efficient investment and capital allocation decisions to accelerate our global growth.

Get to know our Finance team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.

 

What You'll Be Doing

You'll be joining the Finance & Strategy team. We partner cross-functionally to improve the profitability, scalability, and defensibility of our business model, carrying projects from initial conception through to final execution.

Here's what your day-to-day might look like:

  • Strategic Decision Support: Partner with stakeholders across the business to develop new investment decision-making frameworks and drive strategy in a dynamic environment.

  • Growth vs. Profitability: Own complex models and analyses to help the business strike the optimal balance between aggressive growth and long-term profitability.

  • Custom Financial Modelling: Lead high-impact modelling exercises to support key initiatives, sizing new opportunities and building business cases for innovative products.

  • KPI Analysis: Track and analyse key financial and business KPIs to uncover trends, assessing current and future risks while identifying new market opportunities.

  • Process Innovation: Lead special projects to automate and scale our forecasting and reporting tools, ensuring our methodologies evolve alongside the business.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Work closely with operators and departmental leaders to develop new policies and ensure day-to-day execution aligns with our financial targets.

 

What You'll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:

  • Finance Leadership: Significant experience (typically 8+ years) in strategic finance, corporate finance, or investment banking, ideally within a high-growth tech environment.

  • Team Development: Proven track record of managing and mentoring teams; you are passionate about building a high-performing "gold standard" finance function.

  • Influencing Power: The ability to earn the trust of senior leaders and influence strategic thinking across a matrixed organisation.

  • Technical Mastery: Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills with the ability to build robust, complex financial models that distill data into digestible insights.

  • Budget Ownership: Experience owning forecasts and budgets for major functional areas, working directly with operators to hit performance targets.

  • Data Agility: Proficiency in SQL (or a strong willingness to learn) to manipulate large datasets and uncover hidden business insights.

 

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Make a visible impact every day

Your work directly improves experiences for customers, partners and riders.

🌱 Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment

Work close to the market with autonomy, pace and real responsibility.

🧠 Build a career, not just a role

Stretch yourself, develop new skills and grow as the business evolves.

🌎 Deliver together in an inclusive culture

Collaborative, values-driven teams that support how you work best.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find more about how we hire here.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!


Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

data.title: Founding Growth Marketer
data.description:
About SuperchargeMe

SuperchargeMe is one brain for the whole commerce business. Ten products, Ads-IQ, Retention-IQ, Restock-IQ, Stores-IQ, Marketplaces-IQ, Crossborder-IQ, NPD-IQ, Concierge-IQ, Feeds-IQ and Partnership-IQ, share one set of numbers. They don't stop at recommendations: they make the changes too, at the level of control each brand chooses. It works inside Slack, plugs into 100+ tools from Shopify and NetSuite to Meta, Google and Amazon, and is running 23 brands today across paid media, retention, inventory and wholesale, stores, marketplaces, catalog and partnerships.

Every function has a tool. Nothing runs the whole. We built SuperchargeMe to run the whole.

The product is live and brands are paying for it. Getting it in front of the right brands is the next step. That's you.

The role in a sentence

Be our first marketer and own the go-to-market: fill the sales calendar with CEOs, CFOs, COOs, CMOs and VPs of E-Commerce at mid-market omnichannel brands, and grow the brands that sign up on their own.

Where we are

SuperchargeMe is already revenue-generating, with brands paying for it every month. What it doesn't have yet is a way for the next hundred brands to find it.

Who we sell to: mid-market omnichannel brands in the US, UK and EU, selling across their own store, marketplaces, wholesale and retail. Two ways in: brands starting with a single product sign up and get going on their own. Brands that want several platforms working together, with onboarding, book a demo.

There's no marketing team, agency or playbook yet. You start with a live website, a sales deck, a product you can demo, and case studies from our first clients that are being written now. A founding Account Executive starts alongside you, so every demo you book has a closer waiting, while sign-ups go straight into the product.

The story is ready to tell. Brands run ten to twenty tools, each now with its own AI, and none of them agree. We call it the Silo Tax. Naming it, and making brand leaders feel it, is the heart of this job.

The work

  • Set the go-to-market plan: which buyers and markets we go after first, and through which channels.
  • Run paid media yourself across Meta, Google, LinkedIn and anything else that works, alongside email, retargeting, campaigns aimed at named brands, events, and joint marketing with agencies, Shopify partners and systems integrators.
  • Work out which of our ten products to lead with for each type of buyer, and write the messaging for each.
  • Build and look after the route to a demo: landing pages, the booking flow, qualifying questions, quick follow-up and a clean handover to sales.
  • Grow self-serve sign-ups, from the first visit to an account that's actually using the product, including our Shopify App Store listing.
  • Turn our case studies and the founders' experience into posts, pages and short videos.
  • Use our own agents on your campaigns, starting with Ads-IQ on Google and Meta.
  • Report every week on demos, sign-ups, activation, pipeline and what each one cost.

What good looks like

We'll measure you on qualified demos and sign-ups, and the revenue they lead to.

Clicks, impressions and ROAS only matter as far as they get us there.

  • After your first month, tracking is set up properly, you've agreed the list of target brands with sales, and your first campaign is running.
  • After your first quarter, demos and sign-ups come in every week from channels you set up, and you know what each one costs by channel.
  • Sales starts asking for more of one kind of lead, because those are the deals that close.
  • The case studies already being written with our first clients are published, and sales uses them in every deal.

What you bring

  • At least four years in B2B demand generation or growth, ideally at a software company selling to e-commerce or retail brands.
  • You've run Meta, Google and LinkedIn campaigns yourself, including campaigns aimed at a list of named companies, without an agency doing it for you.
  • You can show the pipeline or sign-ups you've been responsible for, and what they cost.
  • You write well enough that a CMO reads to the end.
  • You build your own reporting in the CRM and analytics tools.
  • You already use AI tools and agents in your day-to-day work and can show us how. We sell AI agents, so we'd expect that.
  • You're comfortable being the first and only marketer for a while.

Bonus points

  • You've run a DTC or e-commerce brand.
  • You've built demand from zero at an early-stage B2B company.
  • You've run events or executive dinners in commerce or retail.

Skip this one if

  • Your best campaigns needed an agency to run them.
  • You report clicks and impressions and call it pipeline.
  • You'd rather write the plan than ship the campaign.
  • You want a remote or mostly remote role. We're together in North London Monday to Thursday.

Why join

  • You'll set up marketing from scratch, and you'll have a say in who joins the team after you.
  • Most brand leaders haven't yet seen AI that takes actions on their business. You'll shape how they first hear about it.
  • You'll work alongside both founders, who ran commerce brands before building software. Decisions are quick, and what you hear from the market gets into the product fast.
  • You can use our agents on your own work from your first day.

How we hire

  • A 30-minute intro call with the co-founders.
  • A short exercise: a one-page plan for getting qualified demos from mid-market omnichannel brands and growing sign-ups.
  • A working session with the founders on your plan.
  • References.

What you get

£60,000–£75,000 salary plus bonus

Share options so you own a real piece of what you build. Plus a company car and a strong benefits package.

In person in North London, Monday to Thursday, with Fridays flexible

Own Conveo's data, from the warehouse to the dashboard, and build the team every part of the business relies on.

This role can be based from either our London or Antwerp location.

Conveo is building the AI-powered infrastructure for consumer understanding, making consumer and B2B research fast, affordable and high quality. Global brands such as Unilever, Google and Orange use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across their marketing, product and research teams.

Backed by Y Combinator, we're in a period of rapid growth. We started this year with around 20 people and are on track to reach around 120 by year end, so the people who join now have an outsized chance to shape how the company is built.

We raised a $50M Series A led by DST Global, giving us the fuel to move even faster. We’re investing in our product, growing an exceptional team, and taking on bigger challenges as we enter our next stage of growth.

The Role

You'll be our first Head of Data. You'll own internal data at Conveo and build the team that serves the whole company with it.

You won't be starting from a blank page. Our GTM engineering team has built a data warehouse and semantic layer and has made a start on BI, and colleagues in operations have helped shape our metric definitions. What we don't have is one person who owns all of it, knows what good looks like, and turns it into something every team trusts and uses.

You'll report to our CFO and work very closely with our CTO, as well as with the engineering team, operations and go-to-market. This is a hands-on role. You'll be in the data yourself, not writing a strategy and handing it over. You'll start as the first member of the data team, with a remit to hire as we grow.

This is a role for the long term, not an audit-and-leave project. It starts with the foundations and grows into a bigger team, with room for machine learning and data science to help us predict more across the business.

What You'll Do

Own the data stack end to end

  • Take ownership of our warehouse (Google BigQuery), our transformation and semantic layers (dbt and Cube today) and our BI tooling (Metabase today)

  • Review what's been built with a critical eye, and get it ready to scale as new tools and data sources come in

  • Think through access rights, so it's clear who can see customer, HR and financial data once it all lives in one place

Build one source of truth the business trusts

  • Own metric definitions, so every team works from the same numbers

  • Close the gaps that matter most, starting with areas like marketing attribution and the data our finance team needs for its analysis

  • Make our data reliable enough that people trust it and act on it

Turn data into insight for every team

  • Sit down with department leads, get to the real question behind a request, and build the analysis that answers it

  • Act as the translator between engineering and the business: ask engineers the hard questions about what to build, and explain data in plain English to everyone else

  • Swap today's sprawl of one-off dashboards and AI-generated reports for a clear set of things people actually need to look at

Use AI well, without the slop

  • Shape our data so AI tools can use it reliably

  • Help the business get real value from AI for analysis, without a flood of low-quality output

Build the data team

  • Hire your first team members, and set out what the BI team should look like as we grow

  • Lay the groundwork for machine learning and data science later on

What Success Looks Like

  • After one month: you know our data infrastructure properly and have run a full gap analysis covering what we take in, what we understand and what's missing. You also have a plan for what to fix first and a plan for the team, including your first hires.

  • After three months: you've reviewed the setup in place and own BigQuery, the transformation layer and our BI tooling, and our systems are ready to scale. Teams are already using data better because of work you've delivered.

  • After six months: every department is running with deep insights and analytics, and our leaders have the confidence and ability to use the data themselves.

  • Throughout: people trust the numbers, the business has the dashboards it needs rather than a thousand it doesn't, and we know who the data team hires next.

What You'll Bring

  • Experience leading data at a startup or scale-up, as a Head of Data, Head of Analytics or similar. Ideally you've been at a Series B company or later and have seen what good structure looks like at the next stage

  • Hands-on BI and analytics experience. You've done the insights work, not only data engineering, and you know what good BI looks like

  • Enough technical depth to ask engineers the hard questions, and a clear understanding of how data flows from the warehouse through transformation and semantic layers into a BI tool.

  • A problem solver's instinct: you can talk to a department lead, draw out what they really need, and turn it into analysis

  • A commercial mindset: you understand how a business works and what it needs from its data

  • Strong stakeholder skills. Lots of people will want your time, and you prioritise well while keeping their trust

  • Everyday use of AI in how you work, and a view on how to build data that AI tools can rely on

  • Experience of the challenges that come with scaling fast, and a clear sense of the structure you'll bring as we grow

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience with BigQuery, dbt, Cube or Metabase

Why join us?

  • Work directly with frontier AI models and push what they can actually do.

  • Join a YC-backed team that's growing fast and gives you room to grow with it.

  • Competitive salary (£115k-£130k) and meaningful equity. We want you to own a real piece of what we're building.

  • Offices in London, Antwerp, and New York. We work best together, so we ask for 3 days a week in the office.

  • Regular socials: rooftop drinks, team dinners, run clubs, and more.

  • Twice-yearly off-sites to places worth travelling to. Austria, Las Vegas, and Portugal.

  • Private health coverage with Vitality (incl. dental, vision)

  • Enhanced employer pension contribution (5% employer, 3% employee contribution)

  • Refer someone great and earn up to £5,000.

data.description:
About Conveo

Conveo is the AI research platform enabling fast, affordable, and high quality consumer / B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Orange use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing, product, and research teams.


The Context

Conveo is scaling from $4M to $50M, and the People team is running on goodwill and late nights. We have a recruiting team and a new L&D hire joining, but nobody owns the processes and systems underneath them. Compensation schemes, performance cycles and salary reviews all land on Claudia, alongside the daily operational load.

That has to change before we grow further. You'll be the first dedicated People Operations hire, reporting to Claudia. You'll build the operating system for the whole People function: the tools, data, cycles and lifecycle processes that let us hire, pay, develop and support people well across the UK, Belgium and the US.

You'll work closely with Finance on payroll and compensation, with recruiting and L&D on the employee lifecycle, and with managers across the company. When you've done this well, Claudia spends her time on strategy and growing the team, not on firefighting.

Your Mission

1. Own the People systems stack and make it work across every country

You decide how our People tools fit together, then make them run. Today that spans an HRIS, EOR and PEO providers, and payroll across several geographies.

  • Own the HRIS as the single source of truth for every employee, contractor and EOR hire

  • Lead a possible payroll migration end to end: vendor choice, data cleanup, parallel runs, cutover

  • Manage EOR and PEO relationships across the UK, Belgium and the US

  • Connect systems so data flows once, not through spreadsheets and copy-paste

  • Use AI and automation to remove manual admin wherever it adds no judgement

2. Build an employee lifecycle that feels effortless at 2x our size

Every hire, move and exit should follow a clear, repeatable path that works in any country we operate in.

  • Design onboarding, internal moves and offboarding flows with recruiting and L&D

  • Turn tribal knowledge into documented processes and self-serve answers

  • Keep contracts, documents and policies consistent across geographies

  • Make the experience good for employees and managers, not just compliant

3. Run the people cycles the company depends on

Performance reviews, compensation and salary increases should run on time, every time, without pulling Claudia into the detail.

  • Own the performance cycle calendar, tooling and manager enablement

  • Run compensation projects and salary review cycles with Claudia and Finance

  • Keep bands, levels and approvals applied consistently

  • Spot what slowed each cycle down and fix it before the next one

4. Turn People data into decisions

Leadership should be able to answer people questions in minutes, with numbers they trust.

  • Build reliable reporting on headcount, attrition, compensation and cycle completion

  • Keep People data clean enough to support planning and board reporting

  • Give Claudia and managers the insight to act early, not after the fact

What We're Looking For

Must-haves

  • 5+ years in People Operations, including time at a startup or scaleup through hypergrowth, with hands-on experience across multiple countries (ideally Belgium and the UK)

  • Hands-on experience scaling a People function: you've seen what breaks between 50 and 200+ people and helped fix it

  • Strong systems thinking: you design processes and tool stacks that hold up as the company grows, not one-off fixes

  • Hands-on experience implementing an HRIS (Deel is a big plus) and running at least one people cycle (performance, comp review or onboarding) end to end.

  • Comfort working with data: you can build a report leadership trusts, and you notice when the numbers look wrong

Mindset

  • High agency, low ego

  • A builder first: you'd rather design the system than run the same manual process twice

  • Pragmatic about risk: you treat compliance as a baseline, not the whole job

  • Ready to step up and own things you've seen done but haven't led yourself

  • Calm and organised when several cycles land at once

Nice to have

  • Real curiosity about AI, ideally with automations or AI tools you've already put to work in People ops

  • Multi-country experience, including the US

  • Payroll experience, especially a payroll provider migration

  • Compensation management experience: bands, reviews and benchmarking

What Success Looks Like

After 6 to 12 months, because you're here:

  • Claudia spends most of her time on People strategy and growing the team, not on daily operations

  • The HRIS is the single source of truth, and nobody keeps a shadow spreadsheet

  • Payroll, EOR and PEO run smoothly across the UK, Belgium and the US, with any payroll migration landed cleanly

  • The last performance and salary review cycles ran on schedule, with clear manager guidance and no last-minute scrambles

  • Every hire, move and exit follows a documented process that works in each country

  • Leadership gets headcount, attrition and comp reporting on demand, from data they trust

  • The People operating system is ready for the next stage of growth, and you're taking on special projects that improve how Conveo works

Why Join Conveo?

At Conveo, you'll join a team that genuinely enjoys working, and spending time, together. We care about building real relationships, not just great products. That's why we run quarterly team offsites where we disconnect, reset, and have fun.

  • Own a high-impact role at a hyper-growth, YC-backed AI company

  • Build the People operating system from the ground up, with the room to make it yours

  • Direct access to founders and senior leadership

  • Work with world-class enterprise clients (Unilever, Google, P&G, Orange, and more)

  • Hybrid working model with offices in London, Antwerp, and New York

  • Competitive compensation with meaningful equity upside

  • A culture built on taste, speed, ownership, and ambition

👋 Hey! We're Conveo.ai

Conveo is a Y Combinator-backed company in an active growth period. We started this year as a team of ~20 and are on track to reach ~120 people by year end. The people who join now have an outsized chance to shape how this company is built.

 

We raised a $50M Series A led by DST Global, giving us the fuel to move even faster. We’re investing in our product, growing an exceptional team, and taking on bigger challenges as we enter our next stage of growth.

The engineering team is small and deliberately so. There are no product managers, no designer handoffs, no tickets waiting for someone else to prioritise. Engineers own the full distance from customer problem to working software, and that proximity to the product is exactly what makes this role interesting. You'll report directly to one of our engineering leads, and work incredibly closely with our CTO, Maarten.

Dig deeper into our Engineering/Product ways of working 👉 here 👈


What we're building and why

Conveo is the AI research platform enabling fast, affordable, and high quality consumer / B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Orange use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing, and product teams.

Traditional research is slow, expensive, and superficial. Running it well requires expertise most teams don't have. That gap affects how well companies understand their customers and how well they can serve them. We're closing it.

What you'll do

We need a Senior Product Engineer who works backwards from the experience. This is someone who starts with the user's problem, not a spec, and owns everything between that conversation and the code that ships. You shape what gets built, actively contributing to product direction, influencing what we build and how we build it, with real technical and strategic impact.

Own the full stack, from the interface to the infrastructure

Build the interface customers open every day and can't imagine working without. React is the core of what customers see and touch — you lead frontend architecture in React and TypeScript, set the quality bar for components, state management, and performance. And you don't stop there. From API design to cloud infrastructure (AWS), you ship complete, polished features end to end, including AI-powered ones built on LLM APIs, prompt engineering, and async pipelines.

Be the engineering voice in every customer conversation

When a customer has a need, an engineer hears it, interprets it, and solves it. You join customer calls (about once a week), form a clear point of view on what to build, translate feedback into scoped product decisions, and follow through.

Use AI throughout

You reach for agentic solutions first. You use AI to reason, build, review, and test at every stage and you help raise the bar for how the whole team works. Documentation overhead doesn't slow us down here — AI handles that layer, and you're someone who is happy to work that way. You stay current on what frontier models can do and bring that into what we ship.

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years of experience building full-stack applications with TypeScript and Node.js.

  • Strong backend experience: designing APIs, working with PostgreSQL, and managing background jobs and async workflows.

  • Solid frontend skills with React. .

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS and/or GCP) — you're comfortable with services like S3, media pipelines, and deployment tooling.

  • Experience building AI-driven applications (e.g. prompt engineering, working with LLM APIs, and/or fine-tuning experience are a plus).

  • Can independently lead projects from concept to launch.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English with a keen eye for detail.

  • A collaborative mindset, able to work autonomously in a small, fast-paced team.

Bonus

  • Experience with React Router v7 or Remix.

  • Experience at a small, fast-moving SaaS company where you’ve been client-facing

  • Exposure to market research or qualitative research tooling.

  • You've shipped agentic AI systems to production and can speak to failure modes, evaluations, and tool design.

Why join us?

  • Ship alongside engineers who've built and scaled products used by millions.

  • Work directly with frontier AI models and push what they can actually do.

  • Join a YC-backed team that's growing fast and gives you room to grow with it.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity. We want you to own a real piece of what we're building.

  • Offices in London, Antwerp, and New York. We work best together, so we ask for 3 days a week in the office.

  • Regular socials: rooftop drinks, team dinners, run clubs, and more.

  • Twice-yearly off-sites to places worth travelling to. Austria, Las Vegas, and Portugal.

  • Private health coverage with Vitality (incl. dental, vision)

  • Enhanced employer pension contribution (5% employer, 3% employee contribution)

  • Refer someone great and earn up to £5,000.

#LI-ML1

Compensation: £80K – £125K • Offers Equity

data.title: Operations analyst - Transfers
data.description:
Hybrid with 2 days a week in our Edinburgh or Bath office

 

About us

Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform that’s on a mission to helping more people to invest – and invest well.

 

We’re B-Corp certified with an amazing product-market fit, impressive early traction and the potential to transform an outdated industry, for the better. We've been growing fast and will scale even faster over the next few years.

 

We’re also proud to be part of Octopus, the £multi billion group that's on a mission to breathe new life into broken industries, through companies like Octopus Energy, Octopus Investments and Octopus Money.

 

Check out the Seccl website for the latest on our products and our mission to shape the future of investments.

 

The role

We’re looking for an Operations analyst to join our Transfers team, where you’ll be responsible for processing transfers accurately and on time across multiple wrapper types. This is a fast paced and varied role that will require you to adapt quickly to changing priorities, move seamlessly between different tasks and processes, and stay focused in a busy operational environment.

You’ll balance pace with precision, managing competing demands while consistently delivering high quality outcomes. Working closely with colleagues across Operations and our customer facing teams, you’ll help processes run efficiently and resolve queries and issues within agreed service levels. Alongside day to day processing, you’ll use your operational knowledge and experience to improve processes, reduce risk and support automation, helping us build a more scalable and resilient operations function for the future.

 

On a typical day you will be…

  • Supporting your Senior analyst with regular business reporting

  • An analytical problem solver, delivery focussed and a trusted member of the team, you will support the wider business by answering queries in a timely manner

  • Investigating and taking end to end ownership of our transfer processes. Ensuring issues are resolved in line with regulatory and customer agreed SLAs

  • Reviewing operational workflow and, where possible, suggesting process improvements

  • Working closely with the customer, product and engineering teams to explore better ways of working and to support our scalability

  • Supporting with training for new members of the team

  • Supporting other areas of Operations as and when required

 

This role’s for you if...

  • You have a good understanding of the platform industry

  • You have proven experience in handling transfers efficiently

  • You have the ability to identify, analyse and resolve any complex issues working to strict deadlines

  • You have good domain knowledge of investment platforms, particularly knowledge of the CASS environment

  • You have strong communication and organisation skills with the ability to describe to both technical and non-technical audiences

 

This role isn’t for you if...

  • You rely on a lot of top-down direction. Here, you’ll have a lot of freedom and ownership of your role, and you’ll be expected to shape your own progression

  • You’re not comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Our speed and scalability are what set us apart; you need to be able to act quickly and think on your feet

  • You struggle to follow through on ideas. We value people who do what they say they will. If you care about something, you have the freedom here to make it happen

  • You don’t like change. You’ll get on great here if you relish the ambiguity of rapid growth and are willing to embrace uncertainty

     

What’s in it for you…

 

We offer a generous mix of benefits for the things that really matter to our people, including:

 

💰 A salary between £30,000 and £35,000 – dependant on experience + reviewed annually

🌴 27 days holiday + bank holidays (some can be flexible) + day off on your birthday + three days (full time) per year for Dependant leave

💙 Two volunteering days per year

🌎 Option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year

🌟 Secclbrate - our recognition programme that offers a mix of flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget

🏅 Length of service award – one month paid sabbatical at eight years

✅ 6% employer pension contribution, and life assurance

🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health

👪 Enhanced Parental leave

💻 MacBook and up to £500 home office set up budget

📖 £750 per person learning budget

🌻 Health and wellbeing initiatives including free therapy via Wellness Cloud, mental health support via Headspace

🌱 Strong financial wellbeing focus including access to Octopus Money, Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing offering via Octopus Legacy

🎁 Perkbox – Flexi-points giving you a range of discounts and perks including free weekly coffee, gym and retail discounts

🚲 Access to initiatives like Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing

 

Our culture

 

We're proud to put people first, creating a culture where we truly listen to what matters most to them. Our transparent and inclusive environment encourages diversity of thought, challenge and experimentation.

 

Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team.

Interview process

Interviewing is a two-way thing, and we want you to have the time and opportunity to get to know us, as much as we are getting to know you. Our interviews are conversational, so come with questions and be curious. In general, you can expect the interview process to look a bit like this, (following an initial chat with one of our Talent team):

  • First stage – 45 mins competencies-based interview with the hiring manager

  • Second stage – one-hour technical interview or assessment

     

⏳ We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out and you should expect to hear back from us within one to two weeks of applying.

 

🌈 Our aim is to build a diverse and inclusive company of awesome people, with unique skills, passions and experiences. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

 

If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you!

Compensation: £30K – £35K

data.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Platform
data.description:
Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company, with frontier AI embedded at every step in the production of critical physical products - from creating advanced materials to engineering and manufacturing.

Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system, uniting AI-automated hardware engineering with AI-designed material science to achieve breakthrough real-world performance. We also offer CurieOS to our customers and partners, extending the same platform and workflows that power Orbital Industries to their own teams and products.

We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing.

Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn.

The role

Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced.

The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do.

This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is.

How we work

We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out.

You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production.

What you'll work on first

In your first six months you'll work across the parts of CurieOS that customers have to be able to trust. Like everyone on the team you'll touch most of them, and go deepest where your interests take you:

  • Tenancy, isolation and identity. How CurieOS keeps each customer separate, from shared multi-tenant accounts to dedicated single-tenant deployments. That covers data isolation, SSO and access control. You'll also be an engineering voice in customer security reviews.

  • Release and production. How changes get to production safely: release gates, staged rollouts and rollback, automated smoke tests, on-call and incident response. We ship often, and you'll build what lets us keep doing that without breaking what customers rely on.

  • Agent quality in production. Measuring how well agents perform on real customer workflows, working with our researchers to bring the latest evals into the platform, and using those measurements to decide what is good enough to release. A model or prompt change should have to pass the same gate as a code change.

  • Observability and cost. Knowing the platform is healthy and what it costs. That means SLOs, tracing and alerting, plus cost telemetry and usage metering for every workflow and every customer, so we can see where model and compute spend goes and make deliberate choices about it.

  • Infrastructure and deployment. One standard for how CurieOS is deployed, configured and upgraded in each environment, across our own cloud accounts, GPU capacity and customer-dedicated deployments.

Where the platform is going

Once those foundations are solid, there's a lot to shape next:

  • Traceable results. Provenance for every number an agent produces: which inputs, tools, models and versions went into it, so our users can check it and sign it off.

  • Agent runtime and context. How agents plan, call tools, manage context across long-running work and hand off to people at the right moment.

  • Durable workflows. Orchestration that survives failures, retries and runs lasting hours, mixing agent steps with deterministic calculations.

At Staff level, you'd set technical direction across these areas, not just within one. You'd own one of them end to end, run the design reviews that our research and forward deployed teams build on, make the architecture calls that are hard to reverse, and help shape how we hire and grow engineers.

Our stack

Python services on Kubernetes, running on AWS plus specialist GPU clouds for heavy compute. Strong engineers from Go, Kotlin, Java or a comparable stack will pick up the language quickly. What matters more is that you've run real systems in the cloud.

You'll have most of these

  • Designed and built backend services that other teams or customers relied on, and made the key decisions yourself.

  • Owned a system in production after it shipped: the cloud infrastructure it ran on, on-call, incidents, how changes went out, and the monitoring that told you it was healthy.

  • Built and run something where LLMs do real work for real users, and dealt with the cost, latency and quality trade-offs that come with it.

  • Used coding agents heavily in your own work, with opinions on where they help and where they break.

  • Led a project end to end, made trade-offs you can explain, and raised the bar for the engineers around you.

Bonus points

  • Shipped software to external enterprise customers: SSO, tenant isolation, per-customer deployments, security reviews.

  • Run infrastructure as code at scale, or GPU workloads across more than one cloud provider.

  • Helped a system or a company through a scaling phase, such as a platform going from internal use to many external customers.

  • Worked closely with researchers, scientists, engineers or other domain experts and built what they actually needed.

  • For Staff: a track record of setting technical direction beyond your own team, such as architecture other teams adopted, a migration you led across several teams, or engineers you've grown into senior roles.

You don't need a background in materials, chemistry or engineering. You'll pick up the domain from the people who have it.

Why Orbital

Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company. We put frontier AI into the making of critical physical products, from advanced materials to data-centre engineering. Our research team works at the cutting edge, from universal interatomic potentials to GPU-native simulation, and we turn that research into tools engineers use every day. CurieOS is the platform that brings it together: the AI operating system the whole company runs on, which customers are starting to depend on for their own engineering work too.

Orbital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

data.title: Account Executive
data.description:
Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain?

The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual, and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers, and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion, that can grade, price, and categorise items with just a photo, turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable, and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. We're backed by some of the world's best investors, including a16z, Y Combinator, and HV Capital, alongside world-class angels who helped build Depop, Shopify, and Postmates.

Today, we serve thousands of resellers and retailers across the UK, Europe, and the US. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

We're looking for people who want to build something that matters, and move fast doing it. Sound good? Keep reading.

About the Role

We're looking for an Account Executive to help define and then execute how we acquire our largest customers for the marketplace.

You'll need a genuine interest in fashion, bonus for secondhand and vintage, and the role centres on driving sales with vintage enterprises, brick and mortar stores, and resellers through visiting their stores, calling, emailing, understanding their needs, and building strong relationships.

The ideal candidate brings an entrepreneurial, creative approach to sales and relationship building. You'll be given a disproportionate level of responsibility and the opportunity to drive massive impact in this next phase of growth.

What You'll Do

  • Acquire Key Accounts: Identify, prospect, and close Fleek's largest marketplace customers, vintage enterprises, retail stores, and high-volume resellers.

  • Build Relationships: Visit stores, get on calls, and build deep relationships with buyers. Understand their needs, pain points, and buying behaviour.

  • Define the Playbook: Help shape how Fleek acquires large customers. You're not just executing a sales process, you're building it.

  • Build an AI-Enabled Sales Engine: Work alongside our tech team to build AI-enabled and automated outreach and new business workflows.

  • Drive Revenue: Own and exceed targets. Take a proactive approach to pipeline building across online and offline channels.

  • Collaborate Across Teams: Work cross-functionally with product, operations, and marketing to feed customer insights back into the business and improve the platform.

What You Bring

  • 2+ years of experience in a commercial role at an early-stage startup. You've sold in fast-moving environments where the playbook didn't exist yet.

  • Familiarity with online and offline sales and outreach channels. You know how to prospect, nurture, and close across multiple touchpoints.

  • Experience or appetite to build AI-enabled sales workflows alongside our tech team. You're excited about using AI to scale outreach and automate the new business engine.

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills. You build and maintain relationships naturally. You're comfortable on the phone, in person, and in a cold outreach.

  • Self-motivated and entrepreneurial. You take a proactive approach to driving sales and consistently over-achieve against targets.

  • Growth mindset. You're ambitious, constantly learning, and always looking to improve your processes and systems.

  • Collaborative. You work well across teams and time zones, we have teams in 5+ countries.

Nice to Have

  • A genuine interest in fashion, secondhand, or vintage

  • Experience selling to SMBs, retailers, or marketplace participants

  • Familiarity with CRM tools and sales automation platforms

How We Work

Fleek is an in-office company. We believe the best work happens when people are together: the quick decisions, the cross-functional energy, the ability to solve problems in real time. Most of the team works from our London HQ 4–5 days a week.

We're not prescriptive about it. Performance and trust matter more than attendance. We hire adults and treat them accordingly.

  • Location: London HQ, Heneage Street, E1 (Shoreditch / Aldgate East)

  • Work model: In-office, typically 4–5 days per week.

  • Stage: Hyper-growth

  • Team: 100+ across London, India, and Pakistan

  • Culture: High ownership, non-hierarchical, fast-moving. Founder-led with strong opinions loosely held.

Our Values

Five values shape how we work at Fleek:

  • Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself: Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach.

  • Absolute Ownership: The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done.

  • Curiosity Leads the Way: Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate.

  • Talk to the Customer: Deeply understand their challenges, motivations, and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre.

  • Embrace Diversity: A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter.
